_about: Round 4 of the state finance profile audit (work queue R5), 21 Nov 2026. Every quote was checked verbatim against the page text fetched in this session (fetch log: fetched_at). Applied to app/data/state_finance_profiles.json.

res_assessment_ratio.quote: The assessor shall assess property at its full and true value as of January 1 of the assessment year
res_assessment_ratio.note: AS 29.45.110(a). Assessed value is 100% of full and true value.

comm_assessment_ratio.quote: The assessor shall assess property at its full and true value as of January 1 of the assessment year

annual_assessment_cap.quote: The full and true value is the estimated price that the property would bring in an open market and under the then prevailing market conditions
annual_assessment_cap.note: null means no cap: AS 29.45.110 assesses at current market value each year; no limit on yearly increases appears in AS 29.45.030 to 29.45.170 as read.

uncaps_on_sale.quote: The full and true value is the estimated price that the property would bring in an open market and under the then prevailing market conditions
uncaps_on_sale.note: Moot: there is no cap, so a sale changes nothing; the model ignores this field when the cap is null.

reassessment_cycle_years.quote: The assessor shall prepare an annual assessment roll.
reassessment_cycle_years.note: AS 29.45.160(a), with values as of January 1 of each assessment year (AS 29.45.110(a)).

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: An exclusion or exemption authorized by this subsection may not exceed the assessed value of $75,000 for any one residence
homestead_exemption_rule.note: Corrected from a $50,000 market-value exemption, which appears nowhere in the statute. There is no statewide exemption for all homeowners: AS 29.45.050(a) lets a municipality adopt one of up to $75,000 by voter-ratified ordinance, and AS 29.45.030(e) exempts the first $150,000 for residents 65 or older and disabled veterans.

res_assessment_ratio.quote: III All agricultural, forest, and single-family owner occupied residential property, including owner occupied residential manufactured homes located on land owned by the manufactured home owner, and historic building and sites 10%
res_assessment_ratio.note: Class III (owner-occupied single-family) is 10%. Rental housing falls in Class II at 20%.

comm_assessment_ratio.quote: II All property not otherwise classified 20%

annual_assessment_cap.quote: New rules will cap annual increases in taxable assessed value for Class II and Class III real properties at 7 percent.
annual_assessment_cap.note: Corrected from null (no cap). HB73, Act 2024-344, first applied to taxes collected from 1 Oct 2025. The Department says: 'The limitations will continue through the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2027.'

uncaps_on_sale.quote: When there is a change in ownership, the taxable assessed value will be reset to the true assessed value for the subsequent tax year.
uncaps_on_sale.note: Transfers between spouses or family members for no or nominal consideration, or on the owner's death, do not reset it.

reassessment_cycle_years.quote: Properties are evaluated annually, and the cap is applied when the property

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: H-1 Taxpayers under age 65 and who are not disabled–$4,000 assessed value state and $2,000 assessed value county.
homestead_exemption_rule.note: $4,000 of assessed value is the State exemption; the county exemption is $2,000 of assessed value. Larger exemptions apply at 65 and over or with disability.

AR.host: www.dfa.arkansas.gov (Department of Finance and Administration, Assessment Coordination Division)

res_assessment_ratio.note: Assessment Coordination Division 2025 annual report, 'How are my taxes calculated?': market value x 20% = assessed value, set at state level by the Arkansas Constitution.

comm_assessment_ratio.note: The 20% ratio is the same for all real property.

annual_assessment_cap.quote: The taxable value of a homestead property can only increase 5% per year until the property reaches full assessed value. The taxable value of all other real property parcels, commercial, agricultural, and vacant can only increase 10% per year until the property reaches full assessed value.
annual_assessment_cap.note: Amendment 79. The cap phases in increases from a county-wide reappraisal until full assessed value is reached; it is 5% for homesteads and 10% for other real property, and does not apply to new construction or substantial improvements.

uncaps_on_sale.quote: The owner of real property to whom title is transferred by sale is not entitled to claim any previous limitation on the assessed value of the real property.
uncaps_on_sale.note: The Department says this about the age-65/disability freeze. It does not say whether a sale ends the 5%/10% reappraisal phase-in, so the stored value (true) is not confirmed.

reassessment_cycle_years.quote: With the passage of Act 139 of 2023, all counties will now reappraise real property on four-year cycles.
reassessment_cycle_years.note: Corrected from 3. The report adds that by 2028 all counties will be on a 4-year reappraisal contract; counties used 3- or 5-year cycles before Act 139.

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: Homeowners in Arkansas may receive a homestead property tax credit of up to $500 per year. Beginning with the 2026 tax bills the general assembly has authorized an increase up to $600.
homestead_exemption_rule.note: The stored rule is 'none'. Arkansas gives a homestead tax credit (a dollar amount off the bill, up to $600 from 2026 bills), not a reduction in assessed value; the model has no way to represent a tax credit, so this field stays not confirmed.

res_assessment_ratio.note: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 12-62a(b). Hartford uses a different residential ratio under a separate section.

annual_assessment_cap.note: null means no yearly cap: values are reset at each revaluation and held until the next. A town may choose to phase in revaluation increases (§ 12-62c); that is a local option, not a state cap.

uncaps_on_sale.quote: The town shall use assessments derived from each such revaluation for the purpose of levying property taxes for the assessment year in which such revaluation is effective and for each assessment year that follows until the ensuing revaluation becomes effective.

DC.host: code.dccouncil.gov (D.C. Code) and otr.cfo.dc.gov (Office of Tax and Revenue)

res_assessment_ratio.quote: The assessed value for all real property shall be the estimated market value of such property as of the valuation date, as determined by the Mayor.

comm_assessment_ratio.quote: The assessed value for all real property shall be the estimated market value of such property as of the valuation date, as determined by the Mayor.

annual_assessment_cap.quote: The Assessment Cap currently provides that a property may not be taxed on more than a 10 percent increase in the property’s assessed value each year.
annual_assessment_cap.note: Owner-occupied homes receiving the homestead deduction only (D.C. Code § 47-864). It is given as a credit on the bill; the assessed value itself is not reduced.

uncaps_on_sale.quote: New property owners may receive the seller's cap credit only in the half the property was purchased, provided the credit was in effect in the tax half the property was purchased in.
uncaps_on_sale.note: The seller's cap credit ends after the half-year of the sale; a new owner's cap starts again from the current assessment once they get the homestead deduction.

reassessment_cycle_years.quote: for fiscal year 1978, and for each fiscal year thereafter, all real property shall be assessed on an annual basis.

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: This deduction reduces your real property's assessed value by $95,100.00 for tax year 2027 prior to computing the yearly tax liability.
homestead_exemption_rule.note: Corrected from $87,500 (no source; D.C. Code § 47-850(a) sets $67,500 increased each year by the cost-of-living adjustment). $95,100 is OTR's figure for tax year 2027, read 21 Nov 2026. Assessed value equals market value in DC, so flat_market is right.

res_assessment_ratio.quote: All property subject to assessment shall be assessed at its fair market value as of the date of the most recent reassessment base year in the county.
res_assessment_ratio.note: 9 Del. C. § 8306(a). 100% of fair market value, but as of the county's base year, not the current year.

comm_assessment_ratio.quote: All property subject to assessment shall be assessed at its fair market value as of the date of the most recent reassessment base year in the county.

annual_assessment_cap.quote: All property subject to assessment shall be assessed at its fair market value as of the date of the most recent reassessment base year in the county.
annual_assessment_cap.note: null means no yearly cap: values stay at base-year value until the next general reassessment and are then reset to market.

uncaps_on_sale.quote: All property subject to assessment shall be assessed at its fair market value as of the date of the most recent reassessment base year in the county.
uncaps_on_sale.note: false is right in effect: a sale does not change the base-year value. With no cap the model ignores this field.

reassessment_cycle_years.quote: All real property must be reassessed by the county in which the real property is located at least once every 5 years.

homestead_exemption_rule.note: Stored as 'none'. Chapter 83 subchapter I does not set a general homestead exemption, but no source sentence says there is none, so this stays not confirmed.

FL.host: www.leg.state.fl.us (Florida Statutes, Online Sunshine) and floridarevenue.com (Department of Revenue bulletin PTO 26-21); per-field quotes

res_assessment_ratio.quote: The present cash value of the property, which is the amount a willing purchaser would pay a willing seller, exclusive of reasonable fees and costs of purchase, in cash or the immediate equivalent thereof
res_assessment_ratio.note: F.S. 193.011(1): just valuation (100% of present cash value) is the starting point; homestead assessed value is then limited by F.S. 193.155.

annual_assessment_cap.quote: Any change resulting from such reassessment shall not exceed the lower of the following: (a) Three percent of the assessed value of the property for the prior year; or (b) The percentage change in the Consumer Price Index
annual_assessment_cap.note: Homestead property only (Save Our Homes). The Department's bulletin PTO 26-21 says Amendment 3 (approved 3 Nov 2026) 'Reduces the annual cap on assessment increases for non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%'; it does not change this homestead cap.

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: Increases the homestead exemption for all non-school taxes, exempting assessed value up to $150,000 in 2027 and up to $250,000 in 2028, and adjusts for inflation thereafter
homestead_exemption_rule.note: Set to unknown. Department of Revenue bulletin PTO 26-21 (5 Nov 2026): Amendment 3 (HJR 1-F) was approved by voters on 3 Nov 2026 and first applies to the 2027 tax roll. The stored $50,000 (F.S. 196.031: $25,000 against all taxes plus an additional $25,000 for non-school levies, which the statute now says 'shall be adjusted annually on January 1 of each year for inflation') is the rule before 2027. From 2027 the non-school exemption is far larger than the school exemption, which one flat amount cannot represent.

annual_assessment_cap.quote: Several counties have implemented an exemption that will freeze the valuation of property at the base year valuation for as long as the homeowner resides on the property.
annual_assessment_cap.note: Stored as null (no cap). The Department lists county-by-county base-year freezes for homesteads; no fetched page states a statewide rule, so not confirmed.

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: The $2,000 is deducted from the 40% assessed value of the homestead.
homestead_exemption_rule.note: Corrected from $10,000 to the State's standard homestead exemption of $2,000 of assessed value. The $10,000 figure on the same page is the cap on an income-limited exemption for owners 65 and older (O.C.G.A. 48-5-52). Many counties add their own exemptions.

new.applies_to: county and school taxes (not municipal school taxes or bond debt)

homestead_exemption_rule.quote: Homestead Standard Deduction (IC 6-1.1-12-37) in 2025, $48,000; in 2026, $40,000; in 2027, $30,000; in 2028, $20,000; in 2029, $10,000; Beginning with the 2030 assessment date and each assessment date thereafter, $0.
homestead_exemption_rule.note: Set to unknown. The stored rule was a 1% 'circuit breaker', which the record's own citation (Ind. Code § 6-1.1-20.6, 'Circuit Breaker') describes as a limit on the tax bill, not a reduction in assessed value. The homestead deductions are a standard deduction falling from $40,000 (2026 assessment) to $0 (2030) plus a supplemental deduction of 40% (pay 2026) rising to 62% (pay 2030) of the remaining value (IC 6-1.1-12-37.5, same DLGF form).
